expression.comment: Everything except line comments. Split out from the top-level list so f-string interpolations can reuse it: a `//` inside `{...}` is division-adjacent noise at worst, but as a comment rule it would swallow the closing brace and quote and wreck the rest of the line.

fstring-interpolation.comment: shared {expr} interpolation body for all f-string variants. `meta.embedded.line.jade` sits on top of the enclosing string scope so the theme rule for it can reset the interpolated code back to normal code coloring — without it the expression inherits the string foreground and `f"x = {foo(bar)}"` renders as one undifferentiated orange run.
fstring-interpolation.name: meta.embedded.line.jade

fstring-nested-braces.comment: Balances inner braces — dict literals and struct literals inside an interpolation, e.g. f"{Point { x: 1 }}" — so the first inner `}` doesn't close the interpolation early.

fstring-triple-double.comment: f"""...{expr}...""" — must be tried before fstring-double so the closing triple-quote isn't mistaken for an empty string
fstring-triple-double.name: string.quoted.triple.jade

fstring-single.comment: f'...{expr}...' — single-quote f-strings are equivalent to double-quote ones
fstring-single.name: string.quoted.single.jade

string-triple-double.comment: """...""" multi-line string — must be tried before string-double
string-triple-double.name: string.quoted.triple.jade

string-single.comment: '...' single-quote strings are equivalent to double-quote ones
string-single.name: string.quoted.single.jade

prompt-member-deref.comment: obj~>p — sugar for obj.(?p), a prompt dereference on a member. Mirrors prompt-deref: the ~> gets jade-green, the prompt name gets variable coloring. Listed before prompt-deref and before operators so the name isn't left unstyled and the ~ / > aren't split into bitwise + comparison tokens.

prompt-deref.comment: ?varname — the ? gets jade-green, the name gets variable coloring

exception-catch-typed.comment: catch TypeName binding — TypeName gets type coloring; catch-all `catch e` falls through to the plain keyword rule since bindings are lowercase

decorator.comment: @name or @ns::name preceding fn/async fn/struct/extend, e.g. `@tools::register`, `@route(on = "action")`. Confirmed against jade's own parser_tests.rs (parse_decorators): stacks (one per line), optional (args), positional and `key = value` forms. Ends right before `(` — the argument list itself is left to the normal top-level rules (strings, numbers, operators, nested struct literals all already tokenize correctly there, same as any other call's parens).

function-declaration.comment: fn name( — colors fn as keyword and name as function entity

struct-literal.comment: TypeName { ... } struct instantiation — highlights the type name at the call site, e.g. `Point { x: 10 }`

patterns.comment: prompt keyword — same jade-green scope as ?deref
patterns.name: keyword.other.prompt.jade

storage-types.comment: primitive types used in typed prompts and interface signatures
storage-types.name: storage.type.jade

constants-nil.comment: nil, None, and null are interchangeable spellings of the same absence-of-value literal
constants-nil.name: constant.language.null.jade

patterns.comment: binary integer literal — must precede the generic integer rule so 0b1010 isn't split into 0 + b1010
patterns.name: constant.numeric.integer.jade

function-call.comment: name(...) — every call site: plain calls, `extend`-block methods and other dot-calls (`bird.is_bipedal()`, `math.sqrt(…)`), and the trailing segment of a module-path call like `pkg::helper(…)`. One rule covers all three because `\b` matches after a `.` or a `:` just as it does after a space, so the receiver and the path separators fall to their own rules and only the callee is captured. Deliberately placed AFTER keywords, storage-types, constants and support-functions in the `expression` list: those all match the same bare-identifier shape, so an earlier position here would repaint `if (x)`, `int(1, 6)`, and `print(x)` as ordinary calls. `fn name(` is likewise claimed earlier by `function-declaration`, so definitions keep their own color.

closure-params.comment: Matches |x, y| closure params. Lookbehind excludes alnum/]/)/| to avoid bitwise |. Lookahead requires the content starts with a letter (not a space), filtering out bitwise `a | b | c` chains.

patterns.comment: module-path separator — use std::math, from std::math use floor, @tools::register
patterns.name: keyword.operator.path.jade

patterns.comment: ~> — jade-green like `prompt` and `?`. Must precede the bitwise and comparison rules so the ~ and > aren't tokenized separately.
patterns.name: keyword.other.prompt.jade
